question: Which of the following novels is based on the partition of India and was written by Khushwant Singh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Train to Pakistan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Train to Pakistan** is a novel written by Khushwant Singh.
 
• The novel is set during the partition of India in 1947, a period of intense communal violence and mass migrations.
 
• It presents a poignant and realistic portrayal of the impact of partition on a small village situated on the border of India and Pakistan.
 
• The story revolves around the lives of various characters in the village of Mano Majra, highlighting the human aspects of the tragedy.
 
• Khushwant Singh's narrative style in the novel combines historical facts with fictional storytelling to bring out the emotional and social ramifications of the partition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khushwant Singh** was a renowned Indian author, lawyer, diplomat, journalist, and politician.
 
• He is best known for his secularism, humor, and an abiding love of poetry.
 
• Some of his other notable works include **'The History of Sikhs'**, **'Delhi: A Novel'**, and **'The Company of Women'**.
 
• He received numerous awards and honors, including the Padma Vibhushan, the second-highest civilian award in India.
 
• Khushwant Singh's works often reflect his keen observations on society, politics, and history.
